newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to let insurers invest 5.0 pct funds abroad.
newsitem.headline: Poland to let insurers invest 5.0 pct funds abroad.

text.p: Poland will allow insurance firms to invest up to five percent of their funds abroad from January 1, 1997, a finance ministry official said on Monday.
Anatol Adamski, head of the ministry's insurance department, told Reuters the ministry was already finishing work on relevant regulation.
"Staring from next year, insurers will be allowed to invest some of their funds, but no more than five percent, abroad," Adamski said.
Insurance companies may now invest only in Poland.
